summary:
Public Law 118-1 (H.J. Res. 26) is a joint resolution of congressional disapproval directed at the District of Columbia Council’s Revised Criminal Code Act of 2022, D.C. Act 24-789. Its sole operative provision states that Congress disapproves the Council action enacting that Act, which the Council approved on January 17, 2023, and transmitted to Congress on January 27, 2023, pursuant to section 602(c)(1) of the District of Columbia Home Rule Act.

The resolution does not amend any provision of the United States Code, create any new federal program or authority, authorize or appropriate funds, impose reporting requirements, or establish implementing regulations. Its operative mechanism is the congressional disapproval process provided by the District of Columbia Home Rule Act for District legislation transmitted to Congress. The identified District measure is a criminal-code revision act; the joint resolution applies only to that specified Council action and contains no broader rule of construction or collateral amendment to District or federal law.

The resolution contains no separate effective-date clause, sunset provision, savings clause, exception, condition precedent beyond enactment of the joint resolution itself, or delayed implementation provision. It was approved on March 20, 2023. Its legal consequence arises through the Home Rule Act’s treatment of a duly enacted joint resolution of disapproval for a District act transmitted under section 602(c)(1), rather than through any freestanding codified amendment in the resolution.
